report_name: Karaoke Giant Daiichi Kosho Supplier Breach Exposes 8.7M Customers

attack_patterns.name: Trusted Relationship
attack_patterns.description: The data breach originated from a third-party supplier, Nippon Columbia Group (NCG), which was targeted to compromise data belonging to Daiichi Kosho. This represents a classic supply chain attack leveraging a trusted relationship.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Local System
attack_patterns.description: Malware on the supplier's employee computer located and accessed a file containing customer data that was temporarily stored on the device.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: The malware on the compromised supplier PC may have exfiltrated the customer data file to an attacker-controlled server, although this could not be definitively confirmed.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: Phishing was suggested as a possible initial infection vector for the malware that compromised the supplier's employee computer.

tools.name: RAR
tools.description: The RAR utility was mentioned as a tool that could be used by adversaries to stage and compress data for exfiltration, specifically by creating a password-protected archive.

identities.name: Daiichi Kosho
identities.description: A major Japanese entertainment company and operator of the Big Echo karaoke chain whose customer data was exposed via a data breach at its third-party supplier, Nippon Columbia Group.

identities.name: Nippon Columbia Group
identities.description: A third-party supplier for Daiichi Kosho that manages customer data. A malware infection on an NCG employee's computer led to the potential exposure of 8.7 million customer records.

indicators.name: Suspicious RAR Archiving with Password
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious RAR Archiving with Password
id: 7b9c1d3e-f2a1-4b8c-9e0d-a1b2c3d4e5f6
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of rar.exe to create a password-protected archive, a technique often used by adversaries to stage and compress data for exfiltration.
references:
  - https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/karaoke-giant-data-breach-eight/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-13
tags:
  - attack.t1560.001
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\rar.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - ' a '
      - '-p'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of rar.exe to create a password-protected archive, as suggested in the hunting hints for data staging before exfiltration.

indicators.name: Suspicious Process with Outbound Network Connection
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Process with Outbound Network Connection
id: e8f7a6b5-c4d3-4e2b-8a9f-0c1d2e3f4a5b
status: experimental
description: 'Detects execution of processes often abused by malware, such as powershell.exe or rundll32.exe, that initiate an outbound network connection, which can be indicative of data exfiltration or C2 communication.'
references:
  - https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/karaoke-giant-data-breach-eight/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-13
tags:
  - attack.t1041
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1218.011
level: medium
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
    Initiated: 'true'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects unusual execution of processes like powershell.exe or rundll32.exe making outbound network connections, a hunting hint provided for detecting data staging and exfiltration.
